newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Yearend inflation seen unchanged after power hikes.
newsitem.headline: Yearend inflation seen unchanged after power hikes.

text.p: Electricity rate hikes of nearly 10 percent will cause some price pressure in Brazil, but economists said they would not change year-end inflation forecasts.
"The bottom line is that our overall inflation figure for the year doesn't change. We are still talking about 7 percent inflation," said Marcelo Carvalho, chief economist for J.P. Morgan in Brazil.

Brasilia announced electrical energy tariff hikes of 9.92 percent late Monday. Economists said they had already factored in tariff increases into their 1997 inflation forecasts, adding the electricity hike was not enough to alter their outlook.

"We thought that we would see some kind of tariff increase, either in utilities or in transportation. I am sticking with my forecast for 8 percent inflation this year," said Mauro Schneider, chief economist at ING Bank in Brazil.
Economists noted that the rate hikes would also not lead to a dramatic rise in the closely watched Fipe inflation index for any given month.

"It takes some 20 days for a bill to be paid and the Fipe index is already a four week moving average so for technical reasons the impact will spread over several months," J.P. Morgan's Carvalho said.

The government said it expected the new hikes to impact Brazilian inflation indices in April in the following way: IGP-DI, up 0.049 percent; INPC-IBGE, up 0.514 percent and IPC-Fipe, up 0.3642 percent.
